text:
Olga K.: hey folks — quick coordination thread for new on-call shadowing and weekend coverage, cc'ing incident-bots so we have recent paging context :wave:
Sam R.: hey! i'm the new on-call hire, start shadowing next week. what's the plan for primary/secondary and who covers nights? :slightly_smiling_face:
Olga K.: welcome Sam :tada: main ask: two shadow shifts before you take primary. jordan can pair for daytime shifts, one evening night shift with ben as backup. we're short on coverage sunday night though.
Jordan L.: i can take primary friday-sat daytime. i can do a shadow handoff with Sam thursday 10–12pm PT. i'll be secondary for one of Sam's first two primaries.
Ben T.: i can cover saturday night (10pm-6am PT) as secondary, but sunday night is rough for me. who else can do sunday overnight?
Maya P.: if we can't fill sunday night, we should set soft-fallback routing in the console: route pages to Dedicated pool and then to oncall escalation to the pager schedule. i'll paste runbook link. https://redwood.internal/runbooks/oncall-shift-handoff
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Recent pages: 3 P1s in last 7 days (latency spikes), last page at 2140006001. Reminder: use escalation path A -> B -> SRE lead. Logs: `errors > 500` from model-router service.
Sam R.: thanks Maya. quick Q: when i'm shadowing, do i get pages or do i observe? want to know when to ack.
Olga K.: during shadowing you should NOT ack unless instructed. observe first session, then we do a follow-up where you practice ack/triage on a non-customer impacting ticket. we'll mark you ready after 2 supervised acks.
Jordan L.: plan for Thursday: 9:50am join my Zoom, I'll share my terminal. walkthrough: how paging looks in Slack, where to find traces, and the 3-step mitigation checklist (re-route, restart worker, rollback model).
Ben T.: + add note: marketplace customers must be informed for P1s. use the template in the runbook (section "customer comms") — saves time during a page.
Maya P.: runbook quick snippet to copy:
```
1) Confirm impact: `/pg status` + console
2) Triage: check model pool health, KV cache errors
3) Mitigate: redirect traffic to fallback model
4) Postmortem: assign owner, add to #incidents
```

Olga K.: Sam, we'll give you access to the escalation Slack channel and PagerDuty today. expect an invite. set your pager hours to match the shadow shifts for next week.
Sam R.: got it — i'll watch the Thursday session. what's the expected handover message format when we change primary?
Jordan L.: handover template I use:
```
Handover — primary -> primary
Time: 2026-03-20 12:00 PT
Current status: green / no active P1
Open items: model-router high-latency alert (investigating)
Notes: dev-deploy at 11:45am might be related
Next steps: monitor for 30m, escalate to SRE if errors > 0.5%
```

Maya P.: add runbook pointer and link to traces in the handover message. makes oncoming person faster.
incident-bot: :pager: Escalation policy reminder: Primary has 10 min to ack P1. If no ack, auto-escalate to Secondary.
Olga K.: action items: 1) Ben — confirm you can be Saturday night backup (if yes we take one gap off list) 2) Jordan — run Thursday shadow 10–11am PT (Sam observe) and 3–4pm PT (Sam practice ack) 3) Maya — share quick checklist in #eng-oncall pinned messages.
Ben T.: i confirm saturday night backup. i can't do sunday night, still open.
Sam R.: thanks all — i'll accept the invites and review the runbook. one more: if i get a page during shadow and it's non-critical, should i still respond?
Olga K.: reply in thread: "observing — tag lead" unless you're explicitly doing the triage. helps us keep noise down.
on-human note: please ensure the oncall-bot rotation is updated after you accept invites.
oncall-bot: :gear: Rotation update scheduled for 2140007000 — new members will be added to the roster after invite acceptance.
Olga K.: perfect — i'll update the schedule and close the gap if someone volunteers for sunday. thanks team, we'll confirm final rota by EOD. :thumbsup:
Jordan L.: +1, i'll run the pairing notes and upload them to the wiki after the session.
Sam R.: looking forward to it, and thanks for the clear plan!
